body.statement: For fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1]\) and \(q<\gamma\), both \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_F\) are no larger in order than \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\). Hence Theorem 2 reduces to \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), the Kennedy et al. pointwise-CATE frontier, whenever privacy does not shrink with \(n\).
body.justification: The required special-case reduction checks that privacy does not spuriously degrade the classical fixed-budget asymptotics.
body.gap: This reduction is a consistency check against Kennedy et al., not a separate novelty claim.
body.consumer: It lets applied users recover the established nonprivate benchmark in regimes where privacy is asymptotically free.
